column1: # somfy-rs partition table.
# The only reason this file exists is `rollcode`: the rolling-code store looks
# its region up by label at boot and refuses to run without it
# writing to a compiled-in offset that would silently collide with the app once
# the app grows. See `docs/specs/2026-08-15-config-integrity-requirements.md`.
# `espflash.toml` next to this file points espflash here
# `espflash flash …` from `crates/firmware` writes this table rather than
# espflash's built-in default. Flashing with the default table instead is not
# silently wrong — the firmware reports `PartitionMissing` and stops.
# Everything else is the stock single-app layout. `factory` is 1.9 MB against a
# ~250 KB image
column2: so the table fits any 4 MB board and leaves room to grow;

column1: # `rollcode` sits after it
column3: at 8 KB — two 4 KB erase sectors

column1: # which is the minimum the ring needs to guarantee that erasing one sector can
# never take the newest record with it.
# `wificfg` is the second region with the same shape and the same reasons: the
# Plan 5 configuration store looks it up by label
column2: and it is two 4 KB erase

column1: # sectors for the same guarantee — erasing one sector can never take the newest
# record with it. It is a separate partition rather than more slots in
# `rollcode` because the two have different write rates and very different
# consequences on loss
column2: and one erase must never touch both.

column1: # Note `rollcode` keeps its offset. A board reflashed with this table keeps its
# rolling codes; only the new region beyond it is added.
